subject: Committed pricing & milestone invoicing for multi-year agreement
messages:
From: Kyle Gordon <kgordon@clearwave.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@clearwave.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial pricing questions for multi-year plan

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the call earlier. Our CFO is asking for a proposal that combines: a 36-month commitment, a graduated ramp in capacity across the term, and milestone-based invoicing so we can align payments to delivery and budget cycles. Two specific asks: (1) can Redwood accommodate Net-90 on milestone invoices if we prepay at least 50% of year 1 up front? (2) we need to understand how term discounts change if we move from a flat 3-year prepay to a ramped annual prepay.

Can you send a sketch of options (pricing + invoice schedule) and confirm whether Finance approvals at Redwood are likely for Net-90 in exchange for partial upfront?

Appreciate it,
Kyle
---
Kyle Gordon
Head of Platform Finance | ClearWave Analytics
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Kyle Gordon <kgordon@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Committed pricing & milestone invoicing for multi-year agreement

Kyle —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a concise sketch with three options (attached Excel):

Option A — 36-month full prepay (single invoice at signing): 22% term discount off list, standard 30-day invoice.
Option B — 36-month hybrid ramp (40% Y1 upfront, 30% Y2, 30% Y3): 18% term discount, per-year invoices with milestone triggers; we can consider extended payment terms on milestone invoices.
Option C — Annual prepay with guaranteed uplift (prepay each year with incremental discount): 12% first-year discount, 10% second, 8% third (smaller overall savings but more budget-friendly).

On Net-90: Finance is open to considering Net-90 on milestone invoices if (1) there is an upfront prepay of at least 50% of year 1, or (2) we put the funds into an escrow account or a letter-of-credit that reduces Redwood credit exposure. That would require a short Finance review and an approval box in our internal pricing exception flow.

I[0m've looped in Rishi (finance) and Priyom (legal/sales ops) to fast-track the exception path and SOW drafting. Can you confirm which option best maps to ClearWave's cashflow plan? If you prefer, we can draft a version of option B with milestone definitions tied to technical delivery so procurement can sign off.

Next steps: procurement confirms preferred option, Redwood issues a pricing exception request if Net-90 required, then SOW + payment schedule in DocuSign.

Thanks,
Naomi

--

naomi_feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Committed pricing & milestone invoicing for multi-year agreement

Naomi,

Quick finance perspective: we can entertain Net-60/Net-90 on milestone invoices but only with mitigants. Viable mitigants include: (a) 50%+ upfront payment for Y1; (b) funds held in escrow or confirmed irrevocable LC; (c) an annual true-up clause to reconcile usage against prepay so we don't leave material credit exposure at year end.

For Option B (hybrid ramp) I recommend the following working structure:
- Effective ARR-based list = $2,300,000 year 1 run-rate (for budget example).
- Pricing credit schedule: 40% upfront at signing (invoice 1), 30% invoiced at the 12-month milestone (Net-60/Net-90 possible with approved exception), final 30% at month 24 (Net-30 standard).
- If client requests Net-90 on the middle invoice, require (i) escrow confirmation or (ii) an additional 5% contract holdback until payment clears.

I[0m'll fill out the internal Finance Exception Request Form once Naomi confirms they want to pursue Net-90; legal needs the precise milestone language to attach to the SOW.

Thanks,
Rishi
CFO (acting) | Redwood Inference
From: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@clearwave.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Kyle Gordon <kgordon@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 May 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Committed pricing & milestone invoicing for multi-year agreement

Naomi —

Thanks for the options. Procurement prefers Option B (hybrid ramp) but we need the middle invoice on Year 2 to be Net-90 because their fiscal year ends April 30 and they will only have budget authority then. We can do a 45% upfront instead of 40% to get closer to Redwood's 50% threshold — would that materially change the discount? Also, will Redwood accept a 3-point escrow fee borne by ClearWave to set up an escrow account?

If Redwood requires a 5% holdback, procurement will likely ask for that to be a credit applied at the final invoice rather than withheld in cash. Please advise.

Best,
Alicia
Procurement Director | ClearWave Analytics
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@clearwave.ai>, Kyle Gordon <kgordon@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 07 May 2026 08:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Committed pricing & milestone invoicing for multi-year agreement

Alicia/Kyle —

Thanks for the clarity. Response to your points:
- 45% upfront: that is acceptable and keeps you in the zone for Finance to consider Net-90 on the Year 2 milestone. The change from 40% to 45% will not materially change the headline term discount for the hybrid (Option B) — we can preserve the 18% term discount as proposed.
- Escrow: Redwood is fine with an escrow arrangement; a 3% escrow setup fee paid by ClearWave is acceptable. Finance will still require documentation and confirmation of funds in escrow before we extend Net-90 on the Year 2 invoice.
- 5% holdback: instead of withholding cash we can structure it as a contractual credit applied to the final invoice (agreed). That meets Finance's goal of a recovery mechanism without impacting ClearWave's cashflow.

Next steps I'll take care of: (1) update the attached pricing sheet to reflect 45% upfront and an annotated invoice schedule; (2) ask Priyom to draft the milestone language for the SOW and the amendment to the MSA to capture the escrow and credit mechanics; (3) Rishi to initiate Finance Exception with the escrow docs once ClearWave confirms the escrow provider.

I'll circulate an updated SOW and the pricing workbook by tomorrow EOD. Can we aim to have the ECC approval and DocuSign ready by next Monday?

Thanks,
Naomi
--

Hi all —

Attached: SOW-Milestones_ClearWave.pdf (draft) and Redwood_Committed_Pricing_2026_v3.xlsx. Key legal points we included:
- Milestone definitions: Prod readiness (milestone 1), Data ingestion complete (milestone 2), Performance acceptance tests (milestone 3). Year 2 invoice tied to milestone 2; Year 3 tied to milestone 3.
- Escrow mechanics: escrow provider and deposit confirmation required before Redwood issues Year 2 invoice with Net-90.
- 5% credit: contractual credit appears on final invoice rather than cash holdback; credit is applied only after acceptance of milestone 3.
- Termination clause: if ClearWave fails to fund escrow or misses payment beyond Net-90 + 30 days, Redwood may accelerate remaining invoices (standard cure period applies).

Alicia/Kyle: please review the draft SOW and comment on milestone wording and the escrow provider details. If all good, I will prepare the DocuSign envelope and the Finance Exception packet for Rishi.

Thanks,
